newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - APRIL 21.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The cabinet's new import deposit goes in effect today, requiring importers to deposit one-fifth of the invoiced price of the material into one of the five chosen banks for six months. Cabinet analysts expect the price of imports to increase by three percent.
- Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus does not want to meet Slovakia's demands for the Czech Republic to return its gold.
- Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy expressed his dissatisfaction with the current approach of suppliers towards construction of the Temelin nuclear power plant.

- The current Centre for External Economic Relations (CVEV) will become a new institution, which will have a more in-depth information system for exporters and which should be a basis for building a network of foreign representation.
- Members of the Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) are not very supportive of party chairman Ivan Masek's plans to create a right-wing fraction within the party.

PRAVO - The cabinet is seriously considering dividing the Finance Ministry into two administrations -- the Finance Ministry and a ministry for administrating taxes and customs charges, according to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus.
- According to Deputy Industry and Trade Minister Vaclav Petricek, the impact of the embargo on exports to crisis areas announced by the cabinet will cost about one billion crowns.

- The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) will probably decrease its prognosis for GDP growth to three percent from its original estimate of between four and five percent, according to the vice-chairman of the CSU, Ivan Sujan.
- According to a report from the World Bank, the Czech Republic had the richest economy in Eastern Europe in 1995 with a per capita GDP of $10,000.

- The Defence Ministry agreed on a contract with Aero Vodochody last week for the supply of 72 L-159 aircrafts, which should take place as soon as possible. The original contract was worth 22 billion crowns in 1992.

LIDOVE NOVINY - After arriving in Prague yesterday for a three-day visit, Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin was welcomed by Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus. He then visited Skoda Plzen and met with its director Lubomir Soudek. He said the basic reason for his trip to the Czech Republic is the economy, because it can contribute to relations between the two countries.

- According to the chairman of the railway workers' union, Jaromir Dusek, Transport Minister Martin Riman does not have a chance to decrease the agreed increase in wages for railway workers in accordance with the cabinet's measures for slowing wage increases in the state sector.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to a survey from the agency Factum, almost half of all Czechs support the cabinet's economic measures, while half are against them. Nearly all citizens call for the resignations of Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik and Health Minister Jan Strasky.
- Tatra Koprivnice, part of the Skoda concern, will establish a joint company with the Russian automotive company ZIL for the manufacturing and assembly of freight vehicles.

- Opposition leader Milos Zeman, is convinced that the economic measures the cabinet announced last week are counterproductive and will not revive the economy. He is especially unsatisfied with the planned 7.3 percent increase in public sector wages.
